predecessors.name: Dutch East Indies
predecessors.text: 'every island to the east of Borneo' (Celebes, the Moluccas, Bali and the Lesser Sundas) in 13 autonomous regions; Dutch New Guinea is not mentioned; the union is 308,500 km2 on the grid against the…

successors.name: Republic of Indonesia
successors.text: East Indonesia without the South Moluccas

successors.name: Republic of South Maluku
successors.text: the Moluccas (South Moluccas), where the Republic of the South Moluccas was proclaimed after the cabinet formed in May 1950

ledger.x: 1946: the State of East Indonesia is established on 24 December at the end of the Denpasar Conference (18-24 December) as a Dutch puppet state; 'It comprised every island to the east of Borneo'.
1950: the Makassar Uprising ends on 21 April.
1950: the State of East Indonesia joins the unitary Republic on 17 August, when the USI is dissolved by Sukarno.

wars.name: Makassar Uprising
wars.outcome: Andi Aziz seized Makassar on 5 April 1950; the uprising ended on 21 April.

wars.name: South Maluku rebellion
wars.outcome: The Republic of the South Moluccas was proclaimed after the May 1950 cabinet and the rebellion was crushed in November 1950.

certainty.note: The 13 autonomous regions follow the Dutch administrative divisions of the Great East; the sea frontiers and the border with Dutch New Guinea are not on the page.
